LESSON: COMPOSTING TECHNIQUES ● COMPOSTING METHODS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship
Topic 3.5: Composting Techniques ● Composting methods
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Composting Techniques ● Composting methods, part of Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: Why is composting relevant in soil improvement?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Composting Techniques ● Composting methods together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: learner exhibit leadership skills in carrying out the composting process using conventional and innovative

methods.

● Love: learner demonstrates self-sacrifice by looking for materials for composting and when managing the composting

process to produce quality manure for self and peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Financial literacy: learner develops skills of saving money by learning how to make compost manure for soil improvement

using locally available resources instead of buying chemical fertilisers.

● Social economic and environmental issues: learner conserves soil by applying compost manure to an existing crop

enterprise.

Suggested Learning Resources: Local Composting materials of plant and animal origin, pictures, video clips and illustrations

and samples of compost manure, innovative gardens, applicable tools and equipment such as lightweight garden fork, shovel

with enhanced grip, Adapted computers with appropriate accessibility features, Appropriate applications/ software, Ergonomic

and head operated mouse and footboards, Writing resources, Positioning devices, ICT tools with appropriate accessibility

features, Other related services (physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, learner support)
